# Adversarial review: anchored internal-vowel deletion head (v71 fit, v74 test)

**Verdict:** The failure has a clear operating-point cause. Retained short vowels (S2) score as high as removed vowels on the selected features, and the high threshold that S2 forces leaves almost no removed vowels flagged. The artifacts can't yet tell us whether anchor placement or encoder time resolution causes that overlap.

## 1. What is supported and what is still a hypothesis

**Supported by the artifacts**
- **S2 alone sets the threshold.** On dev, the 99th percentile of S0 scores is 0.208 and of S2 is 0.98695. The threshold is the S2 value plus 1e-5 (`anchored_training_v71/report.json`). At that point P1 recall is 1/93 and P1w is 6/93, while every negative family has 0 flags. The head is set so high that it almost never flags anything.
- **The selected head is essentially "low vowel peak in the gap".** It is `gap_mass4`: peak weights are −1.75 and −2.48, mass weights are +0.14 and +0.24. The positive mass sign is backwards for phonetics. The code computes `gap_vowel_mass` as vowel probability divided by non-blank probability (`anchored_vowels.py`, `measure`), so a gap that is mostly blank can have a high mass ratio while holding almost no vowel. The selection threw out the margin, focal-emission and ownership features.
- **The selection rule doesn't match the gate.** Selection minimised pooled, weighted cross-entropy (BCE) across all families. The gate is the worst family's 99th-percentile tail. Your finding that all 15 CV candidates stay below 0.56 at that operating point means picking a different head wouldn't fix it. The overlap is in the features, not in the choice of head.
- **Margins carry information but also overlap S2.** The "both minimum margins positive" rule, computed after the test was opened, flags 89/93 P1 and 88/93 P1w with 0 flags on S0, S1, S_original and S_world. It still flags 10/88 S2. That is the same S2/P1 overlap seen in another feature space. It is exploratory only (see section 4).
- **The P1u boundary-robustness gate told us nothing.** P1u matches P1 exactly under all three scorers (1, 20 and 89 flagged). Union and intersection are probably nearly the same once the 20 ms agreement gate and the focal-containment check have been applied. Check how often the two removal intervals actually differ.
- **The threshold rests on one or two dev rows.** A 99th percentile taken with `method='higher'` over about 100 S2 rows is roughly the second-largest value.
- **Real speech lands in the same band.** Your confirmed examples and पिढको all score about 98.2–98.6, just under 98.696. The head doesn't separate them, and it wouldn't flag the confirmed ones.

**Cheap check, conditional on a definition I can't see:** if `both_gaps_empty` means `gap_available` is 0 in both probes, those rows have all mass and peak features at 0. They would then all get the same score. Only 1 P1 was flagged against 20 empty-gap rows, so that shared score would sit below the threshold. In other words, the cleanest possible structural deletion would rank below some dev S2 rows. You can confirm this from train/dev data alone by scoring the zero vector with the frozen head.

**Hypotheses, not shown**
- **H1, anchor placement:** the deletion path pushes a short vowel's frames into the consonant spans, so the S2 gap looks empty.
- **H2, encoder resolution:** a 40–60 ms vowel is about 2–3 frames if these wav2vec2-family encoders run at roughly 20 ms per frame (verify `phone_frame_seconds`). Spiky CTC output may not register it.
- **H3, removal leaves vowel cues:** cutting the intersection interval leaves the formant transitions in place. That would explain why only 20/93 P1 gaps are empty.
- **H4, WORLD artifacts:** compressing the whole region also compresses the transitions.

## 2. Is this a valid stress test?

- **P1 (intersection removal) is circular.** The region removed is defined by the same anchor model being tested. "Vowel removed" really means "the steady state between the model's anchors was removed", and transitions may remain (H3). The positive class isn't shown to be vowel-free.
- **S2 is relevant but is being used as an absolute gate.** Native speakers do produce short reduced vowels, so flagging them is a real risk. But requiring ≤1% S2 flags at the operating point, for vowels down to 40 ms, assumes the encoder can resolve them. That should be measured, not assumed. Keep S2 and stratify it by retained duration. The labels describe the manipulation, not whether a listener would accept the vowel.
- **Vocoder matching:** S2 is vocoded and sets the threshold that is then applied to unvocoded P1. P1w fixes this, and it also fails (6/88 on the paired sources), so vocoding isn't the main cause.
- **Source eligibility** keeps only sources where both probes clearly favour the vowel. So specificity holds only for those selected sources (the report already says this).
- **Policy gap:** the train CV already showed worst-family recall below 0.56, so this test result was predictable. Add a pre-test gate on train-CV recall at the hardest family's 99th percentile, and don't open a test set until it passes. The v74 test is now spent: the margin rule was inspected on it.

## 3. One experiment: oracle-placed windows versus anchor-gap windows (train/dev only, no new teacher data)

**Setup**
- Use the existing train/dev S2, P1w and S_world controls. If those control WAVs have expired, regenerate them deterministically with the same code.
- For each source, use the known edit geometry to compute evidence in two windows, with no fitting:
  - **A:** the current deletion-path anchor gap.
  - **B:** an oracle window of the same length in S2 and P1w, centred on the S2 retained-vowel centre and on the P1w splice point.
- Statistic, declared in advance: the same exact-CTC blank-versus-vowel margin, averaged over both probes.
- Also log, for S2, the fraction of the true retained interval that falls inside the anchor gap.
- Report three things on train, then confirm on dev:
  - P1w recall at the S2 99th-percentile threshold (and at the 95th, because of order-statistic noise);
  - paired within-source AUC for S2 versus P1w;
  - everything stratified by retained duration: 40–60, 60–90 and ≥90 ms.
- Add a phonetic-group cluster bootstrap.

**Criteria**

| Outcome | Condition (must hold on both train and dev) | Next step |
|---|---|---|
| **Anchor placement is the cause** (GO on anchor redesign) | Recall_B ≥ 0.80 with bootstrap lower bound ≥ 0.65; Recall_B − Recall_A ≥ 0.25; at least 60% of the top-scoring S2 rows in window A have retained-interval coverage below 0.5 | Redesign how the anchors are placed |
| **Encoder resolution is the cause** (NO-GO on anchor work) | Recall_B < 0.60 overall, **or** AUC_B < 0.80 in the 40–60 ms bin while ≥ 0.95 in the ≥90 ms bin | Either limit the claim to retained vowels of at least D ms, where D is the shortest bin with Recall_B ≥ 0.8, or change the representation. More data alone won't fix this. |
| **The positives are flawed** | Window-B evidence for P1w versus S_world has AUC < 0.95 | Fix how P1 is built (H3) before anything else |
| **Inconclusive** | Anything else | No spending on data or architecture |

## 4. What to claim in tomorrow's research preview

**Can claim**
- A reference-free, local vowel-deletion measurement head was built and frozen before a held-out test on physical edits. It **failed** admission: P1 recall 1/93 and P1w 6/93, with 0 flags on the retained-vowel controls. It was not promoted.
- The reference-conditioned baseline is still the live system.
- Four user-confirmed words are qualitative examples from one listener, not accuracy.
- Processing runs after the utterance ends, not streaming: median real-time factor 0.089 over 8 utterances on local hardware.

**Cannot claim**
- Any accuracy for Hindi-influence detection, or anything about Hindi causing the errors.
- Specificity on ordinary Native speech, or generalisation to other speakers (all four voices come from one TTS teacher).
- The margin rule as a result. It was looked at after the test was opened and fails the S2 gate anyway (11%). Any future claim needs a fresh test with new lexemes.
- Any ability to tell a short retained vowel from a missing one until the section 3 experiment settles it.
